h: Tactics for teams, extras for the city
p: Escape rooms have a funny habit of humbling the cleverest people in the group. The PhD student gets stuck on a simple colour code, while the youngest spots the hidden key straight away. That's the beauty of it: everyone has something to offer. To make the most of your time, search thoroughly before you start solving, keep found items together, and talk through what you've discovered. If you've hit a wall, try explaining the problem out loud. Half the time, the answer comes out mid-sentence.

Oxford's centre isn't the easiest place to drive into, so the city's park and ride sites are your friend if you're coming by car. Oxford station is also a short walk from the Westgate, which makes the train a simple option for groups. Weekends and the end of the university terms are when slots go fastest, so get booked in early if your dates are fixed. Allow a bit of time either side of your game, too.

There's no shortage of things to do once you've escaped. The Covered Market, just off the High Street, is a historic market hall packed with independent food stalls, cafés and shops. Nearby, Radcliffe Square is home to the iconic Radcliffe Camera, with the Bodleian Library close by, one of the oldest libraries in Europe. Families love the Oxford University Museum of Natural History, with its dinosaur skeletons, and the Pitt Rivers Museum behind it, crammed with fascinating objects from around the world. Fancy some fresh air? Christ Church Meadow is a lovely walk beside the river, and in the warmer months, punts can be hired near Magdalen Bridge for that classic Oxford afternoon on the water.
